scholarships.title: University of Copenhagen Danish Government Scholarship

existing.funding_period: per academic year for the master's programme
existing.description: The University of Copenhagen offers a limited number of tuition waivers and grants through the Danish Government Scholarship programme, awarded competitively to highly talented non-EU/EEA students with outstanding academic records. All eligible non-EU/EEA applicants to the university's MA/MSc programmes are considered automatically as part of the admission process, so no individual application exists. The award is granted as a full or partial tuition fee waiver and/or an amount covering basic living expenses, depending on faculty, and is decided on academic achievement alone.
eligibility: A citizen of a country outside the EU, EEA or Switzerland
Admitted to a master's degree programme at the University of Copenhagen
Granted a time-limited residence permit for the purpose of studying in Denmark
Not eligible for a grant under the Danish State Educational Grant and Loan Scheme (SU)
No legal claim to the rights of Danish citizens
Not holding a residence permit under Aliens Consolidations Act section 9c(1) as the child of a section 9m permit holder who is a citizen of a country not acceded to the EU or covered by the EEA
Faculty of Science: first-priority admission plus a bachelor's GPA above 90% to be considered
Second-year scholarships: minimum 60 ECTS in the first year at SCIENCE, registered by 1 September; GPA of 11 or higher on the Danish scale in 2025
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizens of countries outside the EU, EEA or Switzerland admitted to a master's degree programme at the University of Copenhagen who hold a time-limited residence permit for studying in Denmark, are not eligible for SU, do not claim Danish citizens' rights, and are not in the excluded Aliens Act section 9c family-permit category. Selection is on academic achievement only; financial need is not considered.
benefits: Automatic consideration with the admission application, no separate form
Faculty of Science: tuition fees plus living expenses for 22 months
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences: either tuition plus living expenses or tuition only
Limited second-year scholarships: roughly 2 per year in Health and Medical Sciences, and in Science for students with 60+ ECTS and top grades
coverage: Full or partial tuition fee waiver depending on faculty
Some faculties cover basic living expenses; Science covers living expenses for 22 months
requirements: To apply for a bachelor programme at the University of Copenhagen, you must meet specific admission requirements and deadlines.
Be aware, at the University of Copenhagen all bachelor programmes are taught in Danish and require the highest level in Danish or documentation for academic language skills in Danish.
Please check the general admission requirement for your country:
I have a student diploma from a Nordic Country (in Danish)
I have a diploma from an EU/EEA country
All of our bachelor programmes have specific admission requirement, which you need to fulfil.
Please follow this checklist for documentation when applying for admission to a bachelor’s degree at the University of Copenhagen. You must upload the documents on optagelse.dk .
I have a diploma from another country (non-EU/EEA and non-Nordic Countries)
documents: Admission application documents for the chosen master's programme
Time-limited residence permit for studying in Denmark
application_method: No application: all eligible non-EU/EEA master's applicants are considered automatically and nominated students are informed through the application portal
existing.selection_notes: Awarded solely on academic achievement; financial need is not taken into consideration. Nominations are communicated through the application portal, and an awarded scholarship must be accepted within a specified deadline or the offer is revoked and given to another applicant.
existing.best_fit: Outstanding non-EU master's applicants to University of Copenhagen
existing.notes: Faculty terms differ sharply and must be checked individually: Humanities considers all non-EU/EEA applicants automatically with no extra documents; Social Sciences has only about 2-3 scholarships per year and awards only for the September intake; Theology awards only partial tuition fee waivers, generally fewer than four per year, and decides after applicants have been charged tuition; Health and Medical Sciences awards about two second-year scholarships per academic year and expects a GPA of 10 or higher on the Danish scale; Science reports that the 2025 first-year recipients had a minimum GPA of 98% and caps second-year awards at three per nationality. Living-expense components are taxable under Danish tax law for some nationalities.
existing.duration: Master's programme length; separate limited second-year scholarships are awarded by some faculties after the first year
existing.application_period: If you are unsure whether you must pay the application deposit fee, please contact the student guidance before the application deadline.
existing.deadline_display: No scholarship deadline is published and no application exists: 'All non-EU/EEA applicants to the University of Copenhagen's MA/MSc degree programmes will automatically be considered for the Danish Government Scholarship, provided they are eligible. Therefore, you do not submit an individual application.' The operative deadline is the master's admission deadline, and the faculty of theology notes that decisions are generally made after admission offers are issued and that the tuition payment date in the terms-of-payment email, sent around mid-May, must be met.
existing.program_type: Government scholarship administered by the university, tuition waiver and/or living-cost grant

official_details.application_cycle: January 15 (September semester intake); September 1 (February semester intake). For the 2027/2028 cycle: January 15, 2027 (September intake).
